name: Xcode Cloud
author: Enplace
summary: Apple's CI for an app: Enplace sets up its own workflow, starts builds and shows each one.
description: Goes on an app product beside the App Store plugin and uses its bundle ID and App Store Connect key. Connect Xcode Cloud once in Xcode, press Set it up, and Enplace makes its own workflow from the Default one and keeps it right. When the app's Builds come from setting picks Xcode Cloud, it makes the app's store builds with that workflow, whoever asks for them (TestFlight does). It shows the app's latest builds (which workflow, branch and commit, and whether it passed), starts a workflow when you press Build, and shares its runs in the same shape any CI plugin can, so Enplace can show checks wherever they come from.

settings.name: Builds it makes
settings.help: What Enplace's workflow archives the app for, in Apple's words. App Store and TestFlight: one build that can go to any tester or to review. TestFlight internal only: your own team's testers. Don't upload: the build is checked but stays in Xcode Cloud.

settings.name: Branch
settings.help: The branch it builds when Enplace starts it. Blank uses the branch the Default workflow builds, like main.

settings.name: Workflow
settings.help: The workflow the Build button starts. Blank uses the first one that's switched on. Store builds use Enplace's own workflow once it's set up.

settings.name: Issuer ID
settings.help: The same key as the App Store plugin's: set it once, there or here. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API.

settings.name: Key ID
settings.help: The ID of the key you generated there. It needs the App Manager or Admin role to start builds.

settings.name: Private key (.p8)
settings.help: Paste the whole .p8 file, including the BEGIN and END lines.

tools.name: get_ci_runs
tools.description: An app product's Xcode Cloud: its workflows and latest builds (number, workflow, branch, commit, status: queued, running, passed, failed or cancelled).
